audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: The bloom bytearray MUST be exactly 256 bytes (2048 bits). forall (bloom): len(bloom) == 256

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The bloom filter invariant (len==256) is enforced exclusively at JSON-to-consensus conversion time via DecodeHexWithLength(e.LogsBloom, fieldparams.LogsBloomLength). The internal struct ExecutionPayload.LogsBloom is an untyped Go string with no structural constraint at construction time; the constraint only materialises when ToConsensus() is called. For the SSZ ingress path (blocks received via P2P or SSZ-encoded HTTP bodies), length enforcement is provided by the SSZ unmarshaller itself (engine.ssz.go checks size != 256 and the protobuf annotation ssz-size:'256'), forming a second, independent enforcement layer. The FromConsensus serialization direction (hexutil.Encode(payload.LogsBloom)) performs no length check on the outgoing bytes, meaning that if the internal []byte field were shorter than 256 bytes (via a hypothetical buggy internal path), the outgoing hex string would encode fewer bytes. However, no such buggy internal path exists in the reviewed codebase.
state_anomalies_found: ExecutionPayload.LogsBloom is typed as string (API struct) with no compile-time or struct-construction-time length constraint; validation is deferred until ToConsensus() call.

FromConsensus serialization path (all fork variants) calls hexutil.Encode(payload.LogsBloom) with no length assertion on the source []byte; a hypothetically malformed internal bloom would be silently serialized.

Internal construction sites use make([]byte, fieldparams.LogsBloomLength) / make([]byte, 256) without going through DecodeHexWithLength; they rely on the constant being correct, not on explicit validation.
State upgrade paths (capella/upgrade.go, deneb/upgrade.go, electra/upgrade.go, fulu/upgrade.go) copy LogsBloom via payloadHeader.LogsBloom() accessor directly without re-validation.

DecodeHexWithLength has a latent logic issue: the first check (len(s) > 2*length+2) is redundant/misleading but not incorrect — the terminal check (len(bytes) != length) is the definitive enforcement.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: The beacon state field latest_execution_payload_header caches the LogsBloom after every block processed via ProcessPayload -> st.SetLatestExecutionPayloadHeader(payload). The cached value is read by upgrade paths and block processing. If an abnormal-length bloom somehow entered the cache (e.g., via a trusted internal path bypassing ToConsensus), it would propagate to all subsequent state copies and fork upgrade transitions. No actual code path achieves this.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: The LogsBloom value is immutable once placed in an ExecutionPayload proto struct and beacon state. No concurrent writers to a single payload object's LogsBloom field. No race condition risk. The concern is entirely in linear validation coverage, not concurrency.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The primary external ingress paths (JSON HTTP API via PublishBlock/PublishBlindedBlock, SSZ HTTP API) both enforce the 256-byte constraint before the payload enters consensus processing. The JSON path enforces it in ToConsensus() → DecodeHexWithLength(..., 256). The SSZ path enforces it via the SSZ unmarshaller which checks the fixed-size field annotation ssz-size:'256'. An attacker sending either a shorter or longer LogsBloom hex string via the Beacon API will receive a 400 Bad Request response. No counterexample was found for the external attacker-controlled path. All ToConsensus() implementations for LogsBloom consistently use DecodeHexWithLength across all fork variants.
attack_scenarios: Scenario 1 (Short bloom, JSON API): POST to /eth/v2/beacon/blocks with LogsBloom hex string of length 510 chars (0x + 254 hex bytes = 255 decoded bytes). Result: DecodeHexWithLength returns error 'length of 0x... is not 256 bytes'. Request rejected with HTTP 400. NOT exploitable.
Scenario 2 (Empty bloom, JSON API): POST with LogsBloom = '0x'. Result: hexutil.Decode returns empty slice, len check fails. NOT exploitable.
Scenario 3 (Oversized bloom, JSON API): POST with LogsBloom hex > 514 chars. First check in DecodeHexWithLength catches it. NOT exploitable.
Scenario 4 (SSZ path): Submit SSZ-encoded block with 255-byte LogsBloom field. SSZ unmarshaller (engine.ssz.go) enforces fixed size=256, rejects with ErrBytesLengthFn. NOT exploitable.

Scenario 5 (FromConsensus serialization, internal): A beacon node internally calling ExecutionPayloadFromConsensus on a payload where payload.LogsBloom is 255 bytes via a buggy internal path. The serialized JSON would contain a 512-char hex string which would fail the round-trip back through ToConsensus. However, no code path exists to produce such a payload through normal execution since all internal construction sites use make([]byte, 256) or copy from a validated source.

Scenario 6 (Upgrade path): A state upgrade (e.g., Capella to Deneb) copies payloadHeader.LogsBloom() into a new struct without re-validating length. If the accessor returned a non-256-byte slice (impossible in practice since the payload entered consensus only after SSZ or ToConsensus validation), the SSZ layer would catch it at the next serialization point.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: No timing-dependent exploit scenarios found. The validation happens synchronously before any state mutation in all code paths reviewed.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: LogsBloom values from external sources enter via two paths: (1) JSON Beacon API endpoints (/eth/v1/beacon/blocks, /eth/v2/beacon/blocks, blinded variants), where ToConsensus() enforces the length invariant before anything reaches consensus processing; (2) SSZ Beacon API endpoints, where UnmarshalSSZ() enforces it at the protobuf/SSZ layer. P2P-received blocks arrive pre-encoded in SSZ and go directly through SSZ deserialization which also enforces the fixed 256-byte field. The execution engine (EL) itself provides LogsBloom data via engine_newPayload RPC responses, which are trusted internal paths where the EL is expected to provide valid data.
entry_points: HTTP Beacon API: POST /eth/v1/beacon/blocks (JSON and SSZ)
HTTP Beacon API: POST /eth/v2/beacon/blocks (JSON and SSZ)
HTTP Beacon API: POST /eth/v1/beacon/blinded_blocks (JSON and SSZ)
HTTP Beacon API: POST /eth/v2/beacon/blinded_blocks (JSON and SSZ)
P2P gossip: BeaconBlock topic (SSZ encoded, handled by sync module)
Execution Engine RPC: engine_newPayload response (trusted EL side)
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: An attacker can submit malformed blocks via the Beacon API HTTP endpoints or via P2P gossip. However, the validation layers at JSON deserialization boundary and SSZ deserialization boundary independently enforce the 256-byte constraint. An attacker would need to bypass both layers simultaneously, which is not feasible with the current code. Classification is 'defense-in-depth' rather than 'unreachable' because the field flows from attacker-controlled HTTP input through the stack.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant len(bloom) == 256 holds at the consensus layer boundary for all external input paths. The guard (DecodeHexWithLength(..., fieldparams.LogsBloomLength)) is applied identically across all 8+ ToConsensus() implementations. The SSZ layer provides independent enforcement at the protobuf level. Internal construction paths use make([]byte, 256) which guarantees correctness by construction. One secondary observation: ExecutionPayloadHeaderCapella.ToConsensus() at line 480 uses DecodeHexWithMaxLength (not DecodeHexWithLength) for BlockHash, TransactionsRoot, and WithdrawalsRoot — these fields accept shorter-than-expected values. This is an inconsistency but does NOT affect LogsBloom specifically (line 448 correctly uses DecodeHexWithLength for LogsBloom in that same function).
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: bytesutil.DecodeHexWithLength(e.LogsBloom, fieldparams.LogsBloomLength) applied in all ToConsensus() methods; SSZ ssz-size:'256' annotation on all protobuf LogsBloom fields.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: The guards are sufficient for the bloom length invariant specifically. Both JSON and SSZ ingress paths are covered. The FromConsensus (serialization) direction has no explicit length guard, but this is acceptable given the SSZ layer enforces correctness on ingress. The secondary finding of DecodeHexWithMaxLength misuse for BlockHash/TransactionsRoot/WithdrawalsRoot in ExecutionPayloadHeaderCapella.ToConsensus() (lines 480-491) is a separate potential bug out of scope for this property.
edge_cases: DecodeHexWithLength first check (len(s) > 2*length+2) is redundant early-exit but does not cause false-negatives; the terminal check len(bytes) != length is the definitive enforcement.
Empty string input '' to DecodeHexWithLength: hexutil.Decode('') fails with 'hex string without 0x prefix'. Handled correctly.
Nil LogsBloom field in JSON struct: if logs_bloom is omitted, Go zero-value is '', which fails hexutil.Decode. Handled correctly.

ExecutionPayloadHeaderCapella.ToConsensus() uses DecodeHexWithMaxLength (not DecodeHexWithLength) for BlockHash, TransactionsRoot, WithdrawalsRoot at lines 480-491. Those fields accept shorter values. This is an inconsistency worth investigating separately but is out of scope for the bloom invariant.
FromConsensus has no bloom length validation on outbound serialization — acceptable given SSZ enforcement on inbound path, but lacks defense-in-depth on outbound.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The invariant len(bloom) == 256 is consistently enforced at all external ingress boundaries: (1) all ToConsensus() implementations use DecodeHexWithLength(..., fieldparams.LogsBloomLength) for the LogsBloom field; (2) the SSZ path enforces the 256-byte fixed-size constraint via protobuf annotation and SSZ marshaler; (3) internal construction sites use make([]byte, 256) by construction. No exploit path was found by which an attacker could introduce a non-256-byte LogsBloom into the consensus layer. The property holds.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: The bloom length invariant is correctly enforced. Recommend: (1) Adding explicit length assertion in FromConsensus serialization functions for defense-in-depth on outbound path. (2) Separately investigating use of DecodeHexWithMaxLength instead of DecodeHexWithLength for BlockHash, TransactionsRoot, and WithdrawalsRoot in ExecutionPayloadHeaderCapella.ToConsensus() (lines 480-491), which allows those fields to be shorter than canonical length — a potential copy-paste defect.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.severity_estimate: Informational for the bloom invariant itself. The secondary finding (DecodeHexWithMaxLength misuse for Capella header non-bloom fields) would be Medium if confirmed to allow inconsistent state.
